cat > diagnosis.json <<'EOF'
{"spec_element": "invariant",
 "proof_obligation": "preservation",
 "diagnosis": "In Shift, the 'untouched' invariant (line 101) only covers indices i <= j < capacity - 1, omitting the last element arr[capacity-1]. On the final iteration (i == capacity-2) the body copies arr[i+1] = arr[capacity-1] into arr[i], but nothing says arr[capacity-1] == old(arr[capacity-1]), so the invariant at line 100 (arr[j] == old(arr[j+1]) for j < i) cannot be re-established. Fix: extend the untouched-range invariant to i <= j < capacity."}
EOF
sed -i '101s/j < (capacity) - 1/j < capacity/' program.dfy && sed -n 101p program.dfy && dafny verify program.dfy

`program.dfy` now verifies: Dafny reports "16 verified, 0 errors". The command still exited with code 2, but only because of warnings about old-style semicolons and a `null` comparison that can never be false. Those were already in the file, and they don't affect verification.

**What broke:** a loop invariant in `Shift` wasn't maintained by the loop body. The invariant on line 101 says the not-yet-shifted part of the array is unchanged, but its range `i <= j < capacity - 1` left out the last element, `arr[capacity-1]`. On the last pass through the loop, the body copies `arr[capacity-1]` into `arr[capacity-2]`. Since nothing said that last element still held its original value, Dafny couldn't re-prove the invariant on line 100 (`arr[j] == old(arr[j+1])` for every `j < i`).

**Fix:** I widened the range on line 101 so it includes the last element:
```dafny
invariant forall j : int :: i <= j < capacity ==> arr[j] == old(arr[j]);
```

I wrote `diagnosis.json` before editing, classifying the failure as `invariant` / `preservation`.
